title: Rapport ekes out bipolar mania win as lead asset ‘just hits’ in mid-stage trial
snippet: Rapport Therapeutics clocked its second Phase 2 win in 14 months for RAP-219—which the company is positioning as a potential pipeline-in-a-product—this time showing improvement in symptoms of bipolar mania.

title: Eyepoint, Enlivex enact heavy layoffs
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Bonus: Q3 2026 Job Market Update
snippet: In this bonus episode, BioSpace Vice President of Marketing Chantal Dresner and Angela Gabriel, content manager, life sciences careers, discuss how the job market shaped up in Q3 and what Q4 might hold.

title: Lilly puts $1.1B on the line for Hong Kong biotech’s AI drug delivery platform
snippet: METiS TechBio’s AiLNP platform uses machine learning models to develop lipid nanoparticles with potentially better tissue specificity that could enhance a drug’s therapeutic performance.

title: Gilead’s ‘highly competitive’ mid-stage ulcerative colitis data ‘validate’ I&I push
snippet: Gilead’s emvistegrast delivered greater clinical response than placebo, setting up the asset for Phase 3 testing in ulcerative colitis as well as studies in other inflammatory diseases and bolstering the company’s push beyond its HIV portfolio.

title: Report: Biopharma Job Market Report Q3 2026
snippet: The third quarter offered positive signals for job seekers and talent acquisition teams. Explore BioSpace's Biopharma Job Market Report Q3 2026 to get a closer look at hiring trends, workforce reductions and the evolving employment landscape across the industry.

title: Epkinly data only one of Genmab's make-or-break readouts ahead of steep sales erosion
snippet: Bracing for patent losses on its cornerstone product Darzalex, Genmab has bet its future on three cancer programs that will deliver pivotal readouts in quick succession.

title: Sanofi breaks ground on insulin plant after securing German government support
snippet: The European Commission approved Germany’s financial support after assessing the risks of Sanofi stopping insulin API production at the Frankfurt campus.

title: EyePoint will halve workforce, end pivotal wet AMD trials early following second fail
snippet: EyePoint is initiating a strategic review after duravyu failed another Phase 3 trial in wet age-related macular degeneration. Amid significant layoffs and trial terminations, the company is shifting attention to the asset’s potential in diabetic macular edema.

title: Merck KGaA makes noise in hematology with $1.1B Silence buy
snippet: Silence Therapeutics’ lead siRNA asset for the rare blood cancer polycythemia vera has been earning analyst raves in a tight race to challenge Takeda in a potential $2 billion market.

title: As AbbVie’s Crohn’s combo beats Skyrizi in mid-stage test, analysts laud autoimmune vision
snippet: AbbVie’s next-gen dual-targeting therapy elicited higher rates of remission than its IL-23 inhibitor Skyrizi in a Phase 2a trial of Crohn’s disease, leading analysts to wonder if the blockbuster can be outdone.

title: Roche returns to Hansoh with broad $15B ADC deal
snippet: Roche is offering $400 million upfront and over $15 billion in biobucks to team up with Hansoh Pharmaceutical in hopes of developing a portfolio of new antibody-drug conjugates using the latter’s in-house tech.

title: China tightens grip on biotech platform ownership but foreign licensing deals still okay
snippet: The new policy signals an escalation by the Chinese government on biopharma deals but is unlikely to have a major impact given that the vast majority of foreign interest in Chinese biotech comes in the form of licensing agreements.

title: Novartis ends mid-stage Fabhalta study in lupus, insists no efficacy or safety issues
snippet: Novartis will continue to study Fabhalta in other indications, with late-stage studies in two rare diseases—atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome and generalized myasthenia gravis—expected to read out later this year and next year, respectively.

title: Disc’s rebuffed rare disease drug sets up FDA redo after ‘clean’ Phase 3 sweep
snippet: Disc Medicine’s bitopertin—rejected by the FDA in February—significantly reduced levels of a key disease biomarker and significantly increased the time patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria were able to spend in the sun and artificial light.

title: Veradermics’ minoxidil pill improves hair coverage in men in Phase 3
snippet: In the wake of a successful IPO and strong stock growth throughout the year, Veradermics now has late-stage data to support a regulatory package for its hair loss pill.

title: From cells to organoids: Cytokines that shape 3D culture
snippet: High-quality cytokines for organoid growth, differentiation, and expansion.

title: Merck/Moderna, Summit/Akeso and ADCs to headline ESMO 2026
snippet: At the European Society of Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid this weekend, analysts will be watching for detailed data on Merck and Moderna’s personalized cancer vaccine, Summit and Akeso’s PD-1xVEGF bispecific therapy, and a host of antibody-drug conjugates.

title: Should amylin have been obesity therapeutics’ primary target from the start?
snippet: While GLP-1 medicines have become synonymous with weight loss, at least one expert thinks amylin would have been the go-to target if biopharma had been focused on the blockbuster indication 10 years ago. A new wave of therapies is now exploring this potentially gentler mechanism.

title: More arms, more questions: The new challenge in multispecific drug design
snippet: As trispecifics, cell engagers and other complex formats multiply, drug developers are seeking discovery and engineering partners to help navigate an expanding universe of molecular possibilities.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
